{"passages":[{"reference":"19.15","text":"And Simon said, “What then? Although matter is inanimate, does it have a nature capable of producing evil things and good things?”

And Peter said, “According to this argument, it is neither good nor evil, because it does not act by choice, being inanimate and insensible. Consequently, here too one can discern how, although it is inanimate, it puts forth animate beings, and how, although it is insensible, it appears to create skillfully formed shapes, both those of animals and those of plants.”

And Simon said, “What then? If God himself gave it life, is he not himself the cause, being—this matter gives birth—of evils?”

And Peter said, “If God gave it life according to his will, his spirit works upon it, and there is no longer anything hostile to God, equal in power to him, or impossible for him, because everything that comes into being through him comes into being as he wishes. But you will say, ‘He himself is the cause of evil, if indeed he himself produces evil things through it.’ What things, then, will you call evil? Venomous reptiles and deadly plants, or demons, or any other things capable of troubling human beings? These very things—the ..... subtle things—would not have existed if the human being had not sinned, on whose account death entered...... For while the human being existed, reptile venom was not active, the powers of harmful plants were not active, harassment by demons did not occur, nor did any other suffering naturally belong to him. But when, because of sin, he fell from being immortal, he became, as I said, susceptible to every kind of suffering.

“But if you say, ‘Why, then, was human nature made susceptible to death at the beginning?’ I tell you: because of free choice. For if we had not been susceptible to death, we could not have been punished for freely chosen sin, since we would have been immortal. And thus, because of our incapacity for suffering, even if we were evil in purpose, justice too would have been weakened to some further degree, since those possessing evil purposes would have been unable to be punished because of their incapacity for suffering.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"φύσιν ἔχει ἐμφύειν τὰ κακὰ καὶ τὰ ἀγαθά","chosen":"does it have a nature capable of producing evil things and good things","rationale":"ἐμφύειν can describe causing things to grow, engendering them, or producing them from within."},{"source_quote":"οὔτε ἀγαθή ἐστιν οὔτε κακή","chosen":"it is neither good nor evil","rationale":"Matter is treated as morally neutral because it lacks conscious choice, not because its products are denied all harmful effects."},{"source_quote":"τεχνικὰ σχήματα","chosen":"skillfully formed shapes","rationale":"τεχνικός here describes forms displaying craft or art rather than the modern sense “technical.”"},{"source_quote":"τὸ αὐτοῦ πνεῦμα αὐτὴν ἐργάζεται","chosen":"his spirit works upon it","rationale":"ἐργάζομαι with the accusative presents God’s spirit as acting upon or working matter. “Operates it” is more formally direct, while “works through it” would anticipate the following δι’ αὐτῆς."},{"source_quote":"ἐχθρόν τι ἐστιν ἢ ἰσοδύναμον ἢ ἀδύνατον","chosen":"anything hostile to God, equal in power to him, or impossible for him","rationale":"The dative τῷ θεῷ can govern all three adjectives. Thus ἀδύνατον is rendered directly as “impossible for him”; context may imply something beyond God’s power or control, but that implication is not inserted into the text."},{"source_quote":"ἑρπετὰ ἰοβόλα καὶ βοτάνας θανασίμους","chosen":"venomous reptiles and deadly plants","rationale":"ἰοβόλος means poison- or venom-casting, while θανάσιμος denotes what is deadly or death-dealing."},{"source_quote":"ἅπερ τὰ ..... λεπτὰ","chosen":"These very things—the ..... subtle things—","rationale":"ἅπερ is emphatic, while λεπτά may mean fine, slight, delicate, or subtle. The exact five-dot printed gap prevents a secure account of the complete phrase, so “subtle” is provisional and the gap remains visible."},{"source_quote":"οὗ εἵνεκεν θάνατος παρεισῆλθε","chosen":"on whose account death entered","rationale":"The masculine relative οὗ most naturally refers to the human being. παρεισέρχομαι depicts death as entering alongside or intruding; “slipped in” is another possible rendering."},{"source_quote":"παντὸς πάθους γέγονε δεκτικός","chosen":"he became susceptible to every kind of suffering","rationale":"πάθος here includes harmful experiences, afflictions, or suffering, while δεκτικός denotes liability or susceptibility."},{"source_quote":"Διὰ τὸ αὐτεξούσιον","chosen":"because of free choice","rationale":"αὐτεξούσιον denotes self-determination or freedom within one’s own authority. “Free will” is possible, but “free choice” maintains the connection with προαίρεσις."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ αὐτεξουσίῳ ἁμαρτήματι","chosen":"for freely chosen sin","rationale":"The adjective characterizes the transgression as voluntary or self-determined."},{"source_quote":"διὰ τὸ ἀπαθὲς πλεῖόν τι, κἂν τῇ προαιρέσει ἦμεν κακοί, ἡ καὶ δικαιοσύνη ἐξησθένει","chosen":"because of our incapacity for suffering, even if we were evil in purpose, justice too would have been weakened to some further degree","rationale":"πλεῖόν τι is loosely positioned and may mean “somewhat more” or “in some greater respect.” The rendering takes it with ἐξησθένει and preserves its comparative force without supplying an unstated standard."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"οὐκ αὐτὸς αἴτιός ἐστιν ὢν αὕτη τίκτει κακῶν;","issue":"The selected edition’s verified reading ὢν is a masculine nominative participle, but no defensible continuous syntax has been established connecting it with αἴτιός ἐστιν, the intervening finite clause αὕτη τίκτει, and κακῶν. The English mechanically preserves the surviving sequence with dashes but does not resolve it into a defensible publishable translation. The conjecture ὧν would yield “is he not himself the cause of the evils that this matter gives birth to?”, but that conjecture is not the supplied reading and has not been adopted.","proposed_reading":"οὐκ αὐτὸς αἴτιός ἐστιν ὧν αὕτη τίκτει κακῶν;","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"ἅπερ τὰ ..... λεπτὰ","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly five dots between τὰ and λεπτὰ. Its content is unavailable, and no restoration has been supplied; the five-dot gap is retained explicitly in the translation.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"παρεισῆλθε...... γὰρ ὄντος τοῦ ἀνθρώπου","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly six dots before γὰρ. Its content is unavailable and has not been restored. The six-dot gap is retained at the corresponding boundary after “entered,” and the surviving genitive absolute is translated separately as “For while the human being existed.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
